sections.title: De: but
sections.content: *De* means "but". It joins two sentences that pull against each other, and like *mert* it has a comma before it: *Van kártyám, de nincs készpénzem.* (I have a card, but I have no cash.) You know *van* with the possessive ending for having: *kártya → kártyám* (my card), *készpénz → készpénzem* (my cash).

items.english: I have a card, but I have no cash.
I have cash, but I have no card.
The fish is delicious, but expensive.
One has to pay. Here is the bill.
Here you are, this is the tip.

sections.content: *De* contrasts, *és* adds, *mert* gives a reason: *Finom, de drága* (good but costly), *finom és friss* (good and fresh), *finom, mert friss* (good because fresh).
